title: DyTed: Disentangled Representation Learning for Discrete-time Dynamic Graph

problem.claim: Dynamic graph representations need to capture both nodes' intrinsic stable characteristics and time-related dynamic preferences.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally mix stable and time-related information in one representation space, which may reduce explanation, robustness, and usefulness across downstream tasks.

contributions.claim: DyTed is a disentangled representation learning framework for discrete-time dynamic graphs.
The framework combines temporal-clips contrastive learning and structure contrastive learning to identify time-invariant and time-varying representations.
DyTed uses a disentanglement-aware discriminator within an adversarial learning framework to enhance separation of the two representation types.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present DyTed as a novel disentangled representation learning framework for discrete-time dynamic graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on Tencent and five commonly used public datasets reportedly show state-of-the-art performance on various downstream tasks.
The authors report that DyTed is more robust against noise.
The authors describe DyTed as a general framework applicable to existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Unsupervised representation learning for dynamic graphs is an active research area.
Dynamic graphs combine stable node characteristics with time-related dynamic preferences, but existing methods generally mix them in one representation space.
DyTed addresses the problem with separate temporal-clips and structure contrastive learning tasks, plus an adversarial disentanglement-aware discriminator.
The authors report results across Tencent and five public datasets, including state-of-the-art downstream performance and greater noise robustness.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates time-invariant and time-varying information through distinct contrastive learning tasks.

interpretation.claim: When representation factors have different temporal behavior, explicitly modeling them separately may improve task transfer and robustness.

application.claim: For other dynamic data, consider designing learning objectives that separately target stable structure and changing behavior.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that disentanglement improves every downstream task or dynamic-graph setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact datasets, baselines, metrics, noise settings, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or training procedure in detail.
